**Position Analysis:**
- Black knight on b4 is actively placed
- White king on c1 is relatively exposed
- White queen on b3 is within striking distance
- White rook just captured on g5

**Key Move: Nd3+**

This is a royal fork pattern—the knight checks the king on c1, forcing it to move. On the next move, Black captures the undefended queen with Nxb3, winning significant material.

After 1...Nd3+ 2.Kb1 (or Kd1/Kd2) Nxb3, Black has won White's queen—a decisive advantage.

**Coaching Note:**
When your opponent's pieces are loose and your knight has access to central squares, look for checks that force unfavorable king moves. Here, Nd3+ isn't just a check—it sets up an unstoppable queen capture. Forcing moves (checks, captures, threats) often create hidden tactical wins. Calculate what your opponent must do after the check, then exploit the resulting position.
